item.title: Maduro Captured: What Comes Next for Venezuela?
item.description: Maduro’s capture is a significant tactical victory for the United States, the region, and Venezuelans. Whether it leads to long-term strategic gains for the United States and Venezuelans, meaning a return to democracy, will be clear only with time.

item.title: Understanding the Saudi Reaction to the Escalation in Yemen
item.description: The UAE-backed Southern Transitional Council’s capture of two southern Yemeni provinces, as well as Saudi forces’ recent strike on UAE-shipped weapons and vehicles in Al Mukalla, has led to unprecedented tensions between Saudi Arabia and the UAE.

item.title: America Needs Economic Warriors
item.description: "Building an economic warrior class should be a national priority among government, business, universities, think tanks, and philanthropies," warns CSIS’s Navin Girishankar in Foreign Affairs.

item.title: Why Did the United States Conduct Strikes in Nigeria?
item.description: Isolated strikes like the ones carried out by the United States are unlikely to significantly reduce the terrorist threat in the region or reverse Nigeria’s growing insecurity.

item.title: The Golden Fleet’s Battleship Will Never Sail
item.description: The recently announced “Trump” class of battleships is cast as the world’s largest and most powerful ships. But these ships will take years to design, cost $9 billion each, and run counter to the Navy's new concept of distributed operations. They will never be built.

item.title: Ryan Berg in Foreign Policy: Trump’s Western Hemisphere Pivot Is Real
item.description: Americas Program Director Ryan C. Berg contends that if President Trump wants to make good on the new National Security Strategy, the United States must recalibrate its defense posture.

item.title: The Pentagon’s AI Problem Isn’t Algorithms, It’s Evaluation
item.description: Current AI benchmarks were not designed for the realities of war. Without defense-specific evaluation, AI systems risk being deployed without evidence they improve military judgment or outcomes.
